MAED 5021.title: Mathematical Analysis and Its Applications I
MAED 5021.description: This course is an introduction to analysis and its applications. Countable and uncountable sets, metrics, norms, open sets, closed sets, continuity, homeomorphisms, connectedness, complete metric spaces, totally bounded sets, fixed points, compact metric spaces, uniform continuity, category, the Baire Category Theorem, sequences of functions, pointwise and uniform convergence, the space of bounded functions.
cilos: Analyze if a given set is countable or uncountable, construct bijections between two sets, and analyze the cardinality of the Cantor set.

Analyze if a function defined on a set is a metric or a norm, analyze if a sequence in a metric or norm space converges, determine whether or not two metrics or two norms are equivalent, analyze if a metric space is of the second category, and apply the Baire Category Theorem in different contexts.
Analyze if a given subset of a metric space is open or closed, compact, connected, totally bounded, and construct the relative metric.

Analyze if a given mapping from a metric space into another metric space is continuous and uniformly continuous by using different continuity characterizations, and determine if a given map is a homeomorphism.
Analyze if a metric space is complete by using nested set theorem and Balzono-Weierstrass Theorem.
Apply fixed point theorem in the context of differential equations.

MAED 5032.title: Applications of Geometry and Analysis
MAED 5032.description: This course will show how mathematical analysis can be used to investigate a variety of physical phenomena. Kepler's laws of planetary motion will be derived from Newton's law gravitation. Further topics will be the use of differential geometry, in particular Gaussian curvature, in describing space curves and surfaces. Additional topics will be other historically important uses of differential equations, Fourier series and harmonic analysis.
cilos: Formulate the quantities that describe space curves.
Present standard examples of curves that are interesting in high school education.
Formulate a curve as the motion of a point particle.
Formulate the quantities that describe surfaces.
Present standard examples of surfaces that are interesting in high school education.
Formulate arc-length in the language of Riemannian metrics.
Formulate the use of normal vectors and curvature in the description of surfaces.
Apply the theory of curves, and  surfaces to physical problems.

MAED 5033.title: Complex Analysis for Mathematics Educators
MAED 5033.description: This course is about analysis of functions in a complex variable. Topics include holomorphic functions, line integrals in the complex plane, Cauchy integral formula, isolated singularities, Taylor series and Laurent series, residues, conformal mappings, Weierstrass factorization, and the Riemann Zeta function. Applications of these ideas will lead to a broader and deeper understanding about topics in secondary school mathematics, including plane geometry, roots of polynomials, trigonometry, evaluation of series and integrals, and the study of prime numbers.
cilos: Describe the geometry and topology of various sets in the complex plane.
Analyze continuous functions in the complex domain, and solve problems involving continuity and approximation.
Identify holomorphic functions in the complex domain, and characterize these functions using the Cauchy-Riemann equations.
Compute line integrals of complex functions and Laurent series of meromorphic functions, and explain these computations clearly using concepts from complex analysis.
Justify the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra using complex analysis, and explain its implication about roots of polynomials.
Evaluate integrals using the residue theory.
Explain the construction of the Riemann Zeta function, and its relationship with the study of prime numbers.

MAED 5111.title: Classical and Abstract Algebra
MAED 5111.description: This is a course which develops the rigorous definition of real and complex numbers, and various aspects of polynomials.
cilos: Use Peano axioms to define natural numbers and their arithmetic rigorously.
Use the method of Dedekind cuts to rigorously define the field of real numbers.
Define complex numbers and apply them to algebraic and geometric problems.
Describe the connection between polynomials and geometric objects defined by them.
Work with various special polynomials and show a variety of their applications.

MAED 5121.title: Algebra and Its Applications I
MAED 5121.description: This course reviews the notion of groups, rings and homomorphisms and quotient constructions. Applications are then described for finite fields and number theory, and coding theory.
cilos: Formulate precisely the mathematical axioms which a group (and ring) must satisfy.
Derive certain more advanced properties of groups and rings from the axioms.
Identify when a group or ring occurs in a physical or mathematical situation, and infer useful information based on properties satisfied by groups and rings.
Apply algebraic concepts to organize and solve problems.
Explain how abstract algebra is used to solve certain classical questions of geometry and algebra.
Explain how abstract algebra is used to prove certain number theory results, and how these results are used for encryption purposes in modern day communications.

MAED 5211.title: Classical and Modern Geometry
MAED 5211.description: This course is about important ideas in the development of geometry. Topics include logic and axiomatic system, projective geometry, Hilbert’s axioms, hyperbolic models, geometric transformations, hyperbolic trigonometry.
cilos: Explain the axiomatic nature of Euclid’s Elements and its shortcomings and show how Hilbert's axioms provide a rigorous foundation for Euclidean geometry.
Formulate the parallel postulate and explain its role in the development of hyperbolic geometry.
Use geometric transformations to characterize various geometries.
Use hyperbolic trigonometry to study various properties of hyperbolic geometry.

MAED 5321.title: Combinatorics
MAED 5321.description: Topics in combinatorics including counting combinations and counting permutations, generating functions, and enumerative combinatorics. Inclusion-exclusion principle, Polya’s theory of counting, graph theory and applications.
cilos: Explain the reasons behind combinatorial principles and applications.
Design combinatorial problems using the principles taught in class.
Present projects related to certain theorems or problems in combinatorics.
Construct problems to show the usefulness of the principles for teaching purposes.

MAED 5322.title: Methodology of Mathematics
MAED 5322.description: This course is about mathematical thinking in mathematics. One purpose is to show how mathematical concepts, terminologies, formulas, equations, and theories are developed through examples of calculus, analysis, algebra, geometry, combinatorics, and probability, etc. The other purpose is to provide a global picture of mathematics by discussing its foundations, structures, internal relations, crises, and envisions. It is a combination of history, pedagogy, methodology, and philosophy of mathematics.
cilos: Solve problems by the methods of induction, analogy and association.
Apply the methods of axiomatization/foundations of mathematics.
Explain and solve the classical three Greek math problems.
Apply the art of infinity -- the distinction between elementary math and advanced math.
Apply the methods of infinitesimal and integration – the foundation of differential and integral calculus.
Solve problems by the Relation Mapping Inversion Principle.
Analyze problems by the method of Simulation Principle.
Describe interesting stories, events, historic schools and philosophy of mathematics.

MAED 5421.title: Probability and Statistics
MAED 5421.description: This course illustrates how to use statistical and probabilistic techniques with an open source statistics package R to analyze data, especially in education.
cilos: Identify the core ideas on analyzing data.
Communicate effectively the statistical results to both lay and expert audiences utilizing appropriate information and suitable technology.
Apply rigorous, analytic and highly numerate methods to analyze and solve problems in daily life and at work.
Carry out objective analysis and prediction of quantitative information with independent judgement.

MAED 5511.title: Teaching Mathematics in the Digital Age
MAED 5511.description: This course is about the use of various digital tools to produce interactive teaching materials for mathematics and the pedagogical framework of designing mathematics lessons using digital tools that can enhance the effectiveness of students’ learning.
cilos: Apply the theoretical frameworks that guide the process of developing mathematics pedagogy using digital tools.
Use various e-learning tools to design effective mathematics lessons.
Convey fundamental concepts in geometry, calculus, algebra, and statistics with the help of digital tools.

MAED 5611.title: Pedagogy in Mathematics Teaching
MAED 5611.description: This course focuses on intricate teaching methods and best practices in mathematics education. It delves into effective teaching strategies, the application of advanced technology in mathematics instruction, current trends and challenges in mathematics education, and the integration of cultural diversity in the classroom. Designed for educators and those aspiring to specialize in mathematics education, this course aims to enhance their teaching proficiency. Upon completion, participants will have a full grasp of effective strategies for math instruction and will be equipped to design compelling math lessons for their students.
cilos: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of historical and theoretical foundations in mathematics education.
Apply a range of effective teaching strategies and techniques that promote mathematical understanding, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Utilize various digital tools and resources to enhance student engagement and learning in mathematics.
Develop differentiated and inclusive learning experiences that cater to the diverse needs and abilities of students in the mathematics classroom.
Design and implement authentic formative and summative assessments to evaluate student progress and provide constructive feedback.
Critically analyze real-life teaching practices and integrate best practices observed in teaching practice videos.
Create well-structured, engaging, and inclusive mathematics lesson plans that incorporate effective teaching strategies, tools, and assessments.
Engage in continuous professional development, reflection, and collaboration, setting future goals for improvement in mathematics teaching practices.

MAED 5731.title: Problem Solving Strategies
MAED 5731.description: This course covers ways to teach strategies and techniques to students to solve mathematical problems as they appeared in mathematical competitions. It covers many techniques, including transformation methods for solving geometry problems, and graph theoretical methods for solving combinatorial problems.
cilos: Recognize various techniques to solve certain types of math problems.
Present solutions and compare the strength and weakness of the techniques.
Modify problems to create new problems.
Identify conditions in solving problems to investigate further applications.

MAED 5821.title: Topics in Mathematics
MAED 5821.description: This course introduces a selection of topics from interdisciplinary mathematics, which may include mathematical physics, mathematical biology, image processing, etc.
cilos: Apply theoretical knowledge, principles and techniques to mathematical physics, mathematical biology and traffic flows.
Recognize roles of mathematics in solving some mathematical physics, mathematical biology and traffic flows.
Apply various theorems to study ideal mathematical models, such as ideal 2-dimensional fluid flows, ideal electrostatic force fields, steady state temperature, etc.
Present solutions of some physical problems in a systematic way.

MAED 5841.title: Topics in Applied Mathematics for Mathematics Educators
MAED 5841.description: This course introduces a selection of topics in applied mathematics, which may include mathematical modelling, differential equations, data analysis and visualization, scientific computation, etc., and their connections with mathematical applications and pedagogy approaches.
cilos: Identify and appreciate the concepts, techniques and processes of mathematical modelling originated from secondary school Mathematics curriculum.
Appreciate and formulate the use of numerical methods in specific daily life scenarios.
Solve formulated mathematical problems with the aids of appropriate numerical methods and coding techniques.
Interpret the numerical results and compare the strengths and weaknesses of different approaches.
Present standard examples of mathematical modelling that are connected with secondary school Mathematics topics.
Design a method to improve the original technique or scientific model adopted.
Incorporate the mathematical ideas and IT tools into education activities and teaching.

MAED 5851.title: Scientific Computation
MAED 5851.description: This course introduces various case studies drawn from different areas of science to illustrate the use of computers as a problem-solving tool. Each integrates physical principles and mathematical models, as well as numerical techniques and computer implementations, into a coherent perspective.
cilos: Apply theoretical knowledge, principles and techniques to physical problems.
Recognize roles of mathematics in scientific computation.
Implement various numerical algorithms on computers and apply them to real life problems.
Present numerical output from a computer code in a systematic way.

MAED 6980.title: MSc Project
MAED 6980.description: In this course, the student will do a project in an area of mathematics or mathematics education under the guidance of a faculty member. The project either surveys a topic, develops teaching plans and materials, or describes an investigation completed by the student.
cilos: Explain advanced mathematical theories, concepts and principles using precise mathematical language, and identify the applications of this knowledge in different daily life scenarios.
Apply independent judgment to investigative mathematical work or relevant educational materials.
Apply a rigorous, logical and analytic approach to execute tasks and solve mathematical problems.
Communicate mathematical concepts and methods effectively to a range of audiences, both orally and in writing.
Work effectively on a prescribed topic in mathematics or mathematics education, and show the capability of delivering presentations in front of professional teachers or scientific experts.

MAED 6981.title: Independent Study
MAED 6981.description: Independent study of selected mathematical topic(s) under the supervision of a faculty member. Consent of instructor is required, and each student can only study this course for once.
cilos: Explain and apply mathematical knowledge of the selected topic(s) of current interest which may not be covered by existing courses.
Apply independent judgment to investigative mathematical work.
Present findings and solutions in a systematic way.

MAED 6982.title: Future Educators Internship
MAED 6982.description: This course is specifically designed for aspiring educators, providing students with the opportunity to undertake internships in various school settings, including primary and secondary schools. Through hands-on teaching practice, students will gain a deeper understanding of the roles and responsibilities of educators, explore their future career paths in education, and develop essential teaching skills and professional competencies. Graded P or F.
cilos: Explain the connection between basic mathematics taught in secondary schools and more advanced mathematical concepts, fostering student understanding.
Apply problem-solving strategies pedagogically to enhance student engagement and understanding in secondary school mathematics.
Investigate and reflect on additional areas of mathematics and their applications to improve teaching practices and deepen subject knowledge.
